blocks.x: All right, let's see. I think it's going now. Today is September what? Third. Today is September the third, and we're recording today at 1926 Harmony Street. And this is your home. Let's get your name, too. Caribou. And your name?
You said they paraded in the streets huh?

Yeah, Neil O'Brien and he used to advertise the ministers when they come in. Al Jolson, he used to come in here at them times, he'd sing at the Tulane Show. And we had a colored minister, I can't think its name now.
Did you ever see Butter Beans and Susie?
Butter Beans and Susie? Yeah, I know them.
What would they do? I've never seen them in person, I just have their records.

They used to sing blues, dance, crack jokes. They used to play on the Palace Show, which was the lyrics at that time. And they played several other places. They used to have these tent shows come here. Right back there where the Flint and Bridges Hospital is, they used to have tent shows come across in there. And they used to play on them all in tent shoes. And we had another great drummer. He used to play for the Palace. That was Chani.
I know him.
Happy.
Which Happy is that? What did he look like?
A little short, reddish looking fella.
Well you know there's Red Happy now, that's the one you're talking about. But there's another one, plays with the Eureka now?

Well Happy, this Happy is not here now. Yeah. He used to play, he was about one of the next drummers. See what I mean, after Chani. And we had Black Benny, me and him and the band with her. He was a good drummer.
I had three Happys here.
Maybe so but I don't know.
Black Happy, Red Happy and Brown.
That's right.
Black Happy is the one with the Eureka now.

Yeah he plays with Eureka. Well he used to play with different bands, the Excelsior Band and all that. He played with all different bands. He plays now with Eureka Band for us when he would make funerals. Now, then we had, oh Lord I can't recall that. But she was a great singer.
Well let me ask you about some of the singers in general now since you can't hear that name. Do you remember Ma Rainey and-
Ma Rainey, that's who I was trying to call them. Ma Rainey, she used to sing in Tent Shoes. Right here at Tyler Allen and Threat.
Ma Rainey.

Ma Rainey. And oh they had so many of them, used to just play in them Tent Shoes, you know what I mean? Well Ma Rainey was the leading woman at that time. She'd have all the gold pieces on her neck, you know, and everything. Big dog woman. And she was very, I mean she could sing good. Loud. Loud. And uh.
Did she have a microphone in those days?
No, didn't have no mics.
How would they do?
It was on the stage, that's all.
They wouldn't use one of those horns, megaphones, you know what they call them? Well she never did use none.
She just stood up there and shouted.
That's right.

She just had voice to do it. She was good. She had just voice to do it. Now some of them would use mics and some of them wouldn't. You're talking about them horns like. Yeah. Yeah. But she never did use none. Never did see her use a horn. She didn't have to.
She had a big voice. Heavy.
And heavy, yeah. Ma Rainey had a terrible voice. Now we had, oh Lord, I can't just think of all them actors naming. I do know a whole lot of them.
Well what about Bessie Smith and Mamie Smith and Trixie Smith and all those women, they all had Smith names, you know?

Well Bessie Smith, Bessie, I know her and she was a blues singer too. But all them other Smiths I don't know nothing about them. I have heard several of them but I don't know too much about them, you know?
But Bessie you heard definitely, ma'am.
I heard Bessie in person, yeah. I heard Bessie Smith in person. And all these others I haven't been around to them, you know what I mean?
Well how did Bessie compare with Ma Rainey? Would she sing like her or different or?

Well she sang, Ma Rainey's voice was more heavy than Bessie's voice. See, Bessie was a good singer but Ma Rainey had a heavier voice. And which to my knowledge I believe Bessie Smith beat her singing. I think she beat her singing. But Ma Rainey, her voice was so loud and her actions was more, you know what I mean? See, she had more actions.
Well what did she do? Did she kind of? Dance. She danced, don't you?
Oh yeah, she danced. She danced and make actions with all her songs, you know? And I can't think of none of them, so.
Do you remember the one she used to sing, If You Don't Believe On? Love Ya? Yeah, I remember that.
Look What A Fool I'm In? Look What A Fool I've Been, yeah. Let's see, something.
You don't think I'm singing, Look What A Hole I'm In?
Yeah, I remember. Did you ever hear about that? Yeah, that was our main show.
And how did she do that song?
Well she'd make emotions, you know, like she was a gun in a hole or something like that, you know? And like she'd fallen off a log, all like that, you know? I was in motion, she was just good.
What is Fallin' Off Your Log?
Fallin' Off The Log? Well that was some make up they had.
Walk the log, I hear that too.
Yeah, Fallin' Off The Log.
Well it was all wreckage, you know? Yeah, and the Frog. What was a Frog?

Well I never really seen them once, but they used to call it the Frog. There was some kind of hop there. And that was a dance? That was a dance, yeah. Frog. They had another dance they called. What was that dance? It was named behind the I don't want to. Oh yeah, it did try. It did try.
It did try.
It did try. It did try. It did try.
Was there any band that was famous for playing music for these different tunes? Well no.

You didn't have a special rhythm to them? No there wasn't nothing special because all of them could play the same tunes. They could all play that Charleston rhythm? All play that Charleston, all of them.
You know that's kind of a tricky rhythm now. Yeah. People don't play with rhythms.

They don't play it no more like they used to. Yeah they had a stand. You see all those, they got a gang of songs now that they added new parts to it. You see like this Kelly's Love and they added new parts to some of these songs. Yeah like Chris Kelly did that they told. Yeah Chris Kelly added plenty parts to that jazz. I remember Chris Kelly. Chris Kelly he added plenty. Now just like the song The Saints Come Marching In, now they added that into music. See there wasn't a song, there was always a hymn but they added in there and made the music. Boyfriend Street Strut.
You mean the one that the grass bands play now?

Boyfriend Street, yeah. But it used to be named at that time Boyfriend Street Strut. See they had Basin Street Blues, the Basin Street Strut. Well that was kind of fast the Basin Street Strut. Then they had 3 o'clock in the morning blues. That was slow blues. Then they had a...
Oh Lord.
When I, when they hear all be around me I can take all of them, so I mean all of them. But I'm going to get them and put them down in the book because I don't have more time to take them.
Oh yeah.
I got a gang more I can get. I had a book but the book got misplaced. And it would give you most all of them. I have one of them Louis Armstrong's Life books.
Oh yeah that's a good old book.
Yeah well I had somebody misplaced some pages out there.
Well what about the Elks? Are you an Elk? Yeah. And you take care of the place now? Takes care of it now yeah. Tell me who do you think were some of the good grand marshals that the Elks had?
Ace Watson. That was the first one I'd named. That was the best Marshall ever had.
You ever see his picture on that record they have out? Yeah. You know that Eureka has a record out of Blue Collar and he's Ace's only.
Yeah.
See he was not.

Ace Watson. The next one behind him was Johnny Salisbury. He was a good Marshall. He was a good Marshall. And up until late now Alexander he was the next good one. We had another Marshall who died. I can't even think of his name. But he was a pretty good Marshall too.
But what makes a Marshall a good Marshall?

Well from his actions in a parade. See take a grand Marshall. You can be a grand Marshall and have too much rhythm in you. Now the best grand Marshall is the study man. Don't have all that jazz with him. See now I don't call them other Marshalls no Marshalls don't you see. Doing all that cutting up in the street.
You know what I mean.

That's right. And I don't call them no Marshalls. But Ace Watson was the best in the Orleans. Best Marshall in the Orleans. And he was dignified with what he did you know what I mean. And when he brought them funerals out there was a funeral.
Well what makes a Marshall good now? He's got to be dignified. Steady kind of fella. As he walks. Now what has he got to do though? What's his job exactly? I don't know.

His job is commanding his body in the back. To see that they do the right things. And if they get out of order it's his place to go through there and make them line up and get them right and keep them straight. Which he used to do that. But these others don't care though. They get in the front they're gone.
Well who's behind him? Let's see. In the back of him. The second Marshall.

The second Marshall. His second Marshall at that time was old man Alexander. He's dead too now. He's dead too now. He said that was the next Marshall after he died. You know the old man Alexander. Well he dropped dead you know. He was the second Marshall at that time.
He has to look after that and he has the second Marshall to help him.
To help him man.
And he's got behind him. Right behind him would come what? The band or the members?

The second Marshall directs the band. I know. The second Marshall sees the... But now right now how they leave from here. On a funeral the band beats behind Ace. And then the second Marshall takes care of the members. But on a parade it's different you see. The second Marshall has the band. See what I mean? But the grand Marshall beats to the front. Know what I mean?
Know what I mean? Know what I mean? Know what I mean? Know what I mean? Know what I mean? Know what I mean?
Know what I mean?
Know what I mean? Know what I mean? Know what I mean?
Know what I mean? Know what I mean? Know what I mean? Know what I mean? Know what I mean? members. If the band always on a funeral, he was to the head.
Well who tells the band what numbers to play?
Nobody.
Nobody?
No. The only thing he'd do is when they'd get around the church or something he'd blow that whistle for them to stop and sound drums, that's all. But for what they play, they play it they self.
What do they sound? What drums?

What does that mean? What's that mean? They're supposed to play no music in front of the church. If you hit a church spot, well he may blow the whistle for them to stop. See, and after they pass the church, they blow the whistle again for them to start playing.
So just the snare drum would be going while you pass the church?
Yeah, that's all.
And you don't want to interfere with the service going on?
That's right. They went in there with the service.
If there's nobody in the church, would they still play?
Well no. Any church.
Even if it's closed though?

Even if it's closed. They're supposed to respect that church. Now sometimes they do run up on a church they don't know in the neighborhood and they keep on playing behind. They don't know what it's at. I've seen a lot of humbugs like that.
I didn't know what it was all about. Yeah. I didn't know what it was all about. When they hit a spot where the church you see the band just cut right on out.
See what I mean? So uh.
Well let me ask you about the societies and clubs that you belong to. How many of you belong to in your life?
Well in my life I belong to, used to belong to Tisha Mingos.
Tisha Mingos huh?

Mmhmm. Eclipse Aiden Pleasure Club. Frogs. I used to be back at the National Park on Willow in Thuid. I belong to the, used to belong to the bulls. I used to belong to the money wasters. The original spokes. Oh I, uh, Zulus. Yeah Tammany. I used to be in all them things when I had some money. And none of them I didn't used to belong to because I was always in the ballroom business and that made you belong to them because they helped you out. But at that time I had money then. I ain't got no money to take care of all of them now.
Well some of them went down huh?
Oh yeah, a whole lot of them went down.
Which ones went down that you remember?

Well uh, the Eclipse they went down, the Frogs they went down, the Bulls went down, and the Money Wasters went down and come back up again. And uh, and Tammany, uh, they didn't ever go out but they was down, I think they're down now altogether. And the Zulus, they went down. See, and they're down now but what I mean, they get the body of people that perform the carnivals. You see, like any club wanna come in, can go in and help them on the carnival but they had not a big outfit like they used to be. See, see what I mean, at one time the Zulus was independent than the other club. But all them members died out from there. And them did die out there. They're just out and don't worry with it.
I think that some Bethlehem Society helps the Zulus.
The Bethlehem, yeah that's uh, Bethlehem, that's the society from downtown. Yeah, Bethlehem. Yeah, they do, on Connerville, they do help them.
And uh, when they have to have them?

Well, originally, they are, uh, any club can go in. Now, they ask for any club to come help. Even to this, over here, if they wanna turn out with them, they can't turn out. See, they don't pick no, no kind of club not to turn out. Cause you, you got a club that can't turn out on Connerville.
I'm not sure about this, but as I remember, I've been to anniversaries and funerals both, with the Zulus, where they have the Bethlehem with them. It seems strange.
Well, the Bethlehem was a, was a little side club they had down there. And, uh, that club started in, uh, what you call, I think it was, they had a place they called a Tin Top on Padilla and Liberty.
Ten Top.

Franklin, Franklin. I think they had a place they used to call a Tin Top. I think the Bethlehem started in there. And they had another one down there named Clover. The Clover. Remember the Clover? Eh? Well, the Clover used to have meat up in there. It was just a, ballroom, but, uh, that's where they started from up in there. Bethlehem already did go out with Zulu.
Now, the Eclipse, did that have anything to do with Eclipse Alley?

No. No, that was Eclipse Social Aid and Pleasure Club. That was, that was at, uh, Fultz and Ferret. Uh, Buddy Blissett, he was, he was the president of that at that time. At that time we used horses in carriages when they would parade. See, we didn't have no automobiles, they'd use carriages. So, that was back in, oh, way back in 1950s, 60s.
What about people back in those times? Did they bury with a band of music then?

Yep. Bury with a band of music like they do now. Sometimes two bands. Sometimes two bands. According to what the fellow brought. Then way back in them times, the fellow could die on the corner and get buried. He didn't have to worry about no insurance. If he bumped on the corner there, the man pick up money for a band and bury him too. It ain't like today.
Just like this, huh? Just pass it around.
Pass it around. That's right.
What would they pass around? Anything.

Saucer. That's what they most used to pass around. Yeah, they had some kind of, where they'd have a saucer and not a box like they have now. They'd take that saucer and go around and then people would know you would put up money.
They have a box now.

Yeah, a cigar box. Then when they ain't got a cigar box, they have their hand put in their pocket so you don't know where they at. But at that time, when they pick up for the day, they'd give it to them.
Oh, yeah.
Yeah, they'd give it to them.
Then what was what? When they pass that saucer, you could see you were a real sport then.
That's right.
You could see you were a real sport with a $5 bill now.

Well, that's how they used to do. But now in the day, it's kind of different. And it's about all the clubs I can think of. Let me see, we had St. Francis Hall. That was Amelia and Willow. St. Francis Hall. And what club did we have back there? They had a club back there. I can't think of the name of that club. What's back there with the head?
Think of it when this thing stops and write it down. Uh-huh.
Tishomingo, Tishomingo, Tishomingo, Randall.
I told them Tishomingo, Tishomingo, Tishomingo, Randall.
I wonder why they ever got that name. I think that's an Indian name.
I don't know where they got it.

That's a county way up in northeast Mississippi. It's the Tishomingo county. Yeah. And I guess the people in Mississippi got it from the Indian. Did any clubs not use a band when they buried? Any of them have a rule against it?
Well a whole lot of them didn't use bands. And then it wasn't, if the clubs didn't give a band, sometimes it would be up to the family. See sometimes the family don't want no bands.
Oh yeah. I know that. But I mean, say in that constitution.
Well yeah, there was a very, a whole lot of them didn't give a band. Because they just turned out and committed, you know what I mean?
I guess Masons and Oddfellas both use music now.
Well they use it if the family want it, but if they don't want it, they don't use it. They use a committee. See plenty of people don't like no band, they just use a committee.
I wonder what the richest society in town.
Well you got me there now. I wonder. I wonder. Some of them are going down. I don't know. I don't know which is the richest one now. I don't know.
The oldest one in town is about to go down. They say that the inseparable friends are the oldest one that's still in existence today. And that's about to go down. It's down by La Fats.
Yeah, that's, that's, oh Lord, let me call that name.
Noah Cook.
Yeah. Noah Cook. The Spanish American. The Spanish American, yeah.
The Spanish American one with Ms. Diggs.
Yeah.
Well it's saying the sound, that should be a rich club. They've been doing well.
Yeah, but they out. They've been sold out. They have that hall last year.
They have, yeah. Somebody else down by the Sanchez.

Somebody else got it. Just the Sanchez Center. The original Sanchez Center sold out. They went out of business. Because the heads took all the money and they turned it over to somebody else, but they still used Sanchez Center's name, I think.
What did they do? They swooped the scene with the money?
Yes, indeed.
That's what happened to the Bulls.

That's what happened to the Bulls. The same thing. That's what happened. And now I think on this last deal, I don't know, I'm not sure. But I think that with the help of Duke of Chase and all of them, they got Sanchez back.
Which got back?
Sanchez Center's. But I mean, somebody else got it. It's not the same original set up. Yeah.

Some group they had, and I don't know what they called themselves. I know what they were. But down at the Big 25, they had a club down there and one of those head sports, you know, took off for California with all the money. I can't think of the name of that one. Baby Dog. Baby Dog. Baby Dog.
Baby Dog. Baby Dog. Baby Dog.
No, they don't call them. Baby Dog.
Baby Dog. Baby Dog.
Baby Dog. Baby Dog. Baby Dog. I don't think I see any Baby Dog. No, they don't come out no more. You see a few of them. You see about five or six of them sometime on the count of the mass.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. They still did it all.
They still did it.
That's about all I can think of.
Well I'll put some more questions to you then. Did you ever go downtown to any of the halls?
Yeah, I used to bum, that's where I used to bum it. Economy Hall. Winter Garden.
Where was the Winter Garden?
Winter Garden was on Ramport in Grabbie. Front, back, downtown side.
That's what the Knights of Pithy?
No, Knights of Pithy was at Franklin. It was named Franklin then.
Yeah, right when the Royal Garden was on Grabbie.
Winter Garden was on?
Winter Garden.
Right at the Royal Garden, he called it the Royal Garden.
Royal Garden and the Winter Garden was the same thing.
Yeah, same thing. And you got me all confused.
What was the one that was across the street from the Astoria? That was the Pelican.
Uh-huh.
Now I'm straight. Pelican. You thought the Royal Garden was on the road too?

No, see, Farbacker was on the Pelican, used to own the Winter Garden too, where they called it the Royal Garden when they got ready. But the original name was the Royal Garden, they called it the Winter Garden. Because it was a good place to go in the winter. See, the temple used to be closed in the winter, so they called that the Winter Garden.
Well why was the temple closed?
Well, I don't know, it was some kind of, upsets in the Knights of Peethers.
Well what I was thinking was they had a roof thing.
The roof, they called that the roof garden.
Would it be cold up there or would it have a roof on it?
No, it didn't have no roof on it. It was on top of the roof.
It would be cold then in the winter.
Oh, in the wintertime, yeah. You didn't have no dances too much up there in the winter.
I see.
Man, right off where the money's at?
Yeah, green, yeah. That's a wonderful spot they lost. Yeah, that's a wonderful spot.
What bands played in those different places like the Winter Garden and the Knights of Peethers?

Well, up on the Winter Garden, I mean on the Temple Root, Desvee used to play up there, Joe Rootby Show. There was too many bands played up on top of there unless some other club would give it and they'd get another band. But Rootby Show and Desvee was the only two played up there.
Was it named the San Suu and Sin Caracal?
Hmm?
San Suu and Sin Caracal?
No, we didn't get to that one.
Who played at the San Suu? San Suu, Buddy P.T. and all the bands. Just any of them. That's over on Howard Street and they still have the sign over there? Yeah, right next to the nightclub over there.
Is it near the Doudrop? Right next to the Doudrop.
That's the one I'm thinking about. Next to the Doudrop. Doudrop.
You've seen that sign, haven't you, Crawford? Which one is that? Put your name on there while you're at it.
Tell me your name. My name is Crawford Lawson Crawford.
Oh good, we gotta have everybody's name down.
Yeah.
Which sign do you mean? Right next to the Doudrop, the San Suu sign?
Yeah, that's the San Suu sign.
We'll pass that many a time.
And we had another one in the Palm Garden. Where was that? Right down there in Ramport between six and seven.
And who was there?
Hmm?
Who was there?
Well different bands, didn't have no special bands to play there. But I think, what you call them, Punch used to play there all the time. And Buddy P.T. And Buddy P.T. Punch and Buddy P.T.
And Buddy P.T. It was available for clubs. You could ring, you know, whatever band you wanted. Yeah, yeah.
You wanted that. See? And I don't know.
Well you didn't tell me who was at the Economy Hall.

Oh, Economy Hall, well Kid Aria and Yurica Band, all bands. They did different clubs would give it, they'd have different bands. They didn't have no special bands. Same way with the Economy Hall, same way. See, we had the Economy Hall and what's that? Co-operators. Co-operators, yeah. And then we had this Franz Amir, the Franz Amir Hall. That's the whole way nobody ducked like me and you couldn't go in there. Creoles. Creoles, yeah.
Well I think that's about the end of the tape here, so we'll put the ladies to talk in the next pace. Oh, I don't talk now. You talked now? We're speaking.
Well I have questions.
Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy. Howdy.

segments.title: Recording opening at Harmony Street
segments.summary: The interviewer announces the date and the recording location, the interviewee's home.

segments.title: Minstrel and tent shows, Butter Beans and Susie, Palace drummers
segments.summary: Archie Martin recalls minstrel advertising, Al Jolson, Butter Beans and Susie, tent shows, and the drummers at the Palace including the various Happys.

segments.title: Ma Rainey singing in the tent shows
segments.summary: He describes Ma Rainey's big voice, her gold jewelry, and singing without a microphone.

segments.title: Bessie Smith compared with Ma Rainey
segments.summary: He heard Bessie Smith in person and compares her singing to Ma Rainey's heavier voice and stage actions.

segments.title: Ma Rainey's songs and dances like the Frog
segments.summary: They discuss a Ma Rainey song, Fallin' Off the Log, and the Frog dance.

segments.title: Charleston rhythm, added song parts and old repertoire
segments.summary: All bands played the same tunes; Chris Kelly added parts to songs, and he lists old titles like Basin Street Strut and his lost book.

segments.title: The best grand marshals of the Elks
segments.summary: He names Ace Watson, Johnny Salisbury and Alexander as good marshals and says a good marshal is dignified and keeps the body in order.

segments.title: Second marshal and order of the funeral procession
segments.summary: He explains the second marshal's duties and how band and members line up in funerals versus parades.

segments.title: Who calls the tunes and not playing past churches
segments.summary: Nobody tells the band what to play; the marshal's whistle stops the band at churches, leaving only snare drum, out of respect.

segments.title: Social clubs he belonged to and which declined
segments.summary: He lists the clubs he belonged to while in the ballroom business, which ones went down, and the Zulus, Bethlehem and Eclipse.

segments.title: Burying with a band and passing the saucer
segments.summary: In earlier times people were buried with a band paid for by passing a saucer, now a cigar box.

segments.title: More clubs and whether societies used bands
segments.summary: He recalls St. Francis Hall and Tishomingo, and says many societies left band use to the family.

segments.title: Richest and oldest societies and halls sold out
segments.summary: They discuss societies losing halls and money, the Sanchez Center, the Bulls and a stolen treasury.

segments.title: Winter Garden, Royal Garden and the temple roof garden
segments.summary: They sort out the downtown halls, the Winter Garden, Pelican and Knights of Pythias temple roof garden.

segments.title: Bands on the temple roof and at the Sans Souci
segments.summary: Robichaux and Desvigne played the roof; the Sans Souci hosted Buddy Petit and others; the sign still stands.

segments.title: Palm Garden, Economy Hall and tape end
segments.summary: Bands at the Palm Garden and Economy Hall were hired by the clubs; the tape ends.
